  Numbers (544 bits each): stage-0 rck insertion TT 804-862, FF 654-706 (the whole 14,740-sink pma_rck tree is that deep: 186 ps of wire buffers from the far pin, 93 ps root, a 7x BUFx24 balancing chain ~210 ps that feeds 11,318 sinks incl. u_dec, then 9 levels) [CHECKED f1c.log]. pma_rx->l0, default next-edge relation: setup TT +1365.59, hold TT -973.48 / FF -820.66 (matches Codex). Hops: l0->l1 hold TT -1.6 / FF -16.2, l1->l2 -14.0 / -29.8, l2->q +2.1 / -12.2, q->any -2.2 / -13.9; all hop setups >= +461 TT. So the hops are normal small hold repair; only the face is wrong.
  Finding: the face fails because the sample point is in the wrong place in the data eye, not because insertion is "too big". Data from launch k is stable from k*833+197 to k*833+763 TT (budget + input buffer). With insertion ~830 the l0 flop samples at (k+1)*833+~30: inside the transition of launch k+1. Timed on the SAME edge (set_multicycle_path 0 -setup from pma_rx, hold moves to -1), measured: TT setup +532.59, FF hold +12.34, but TT hold -140.48 [CHECKED F1 SAMEEDGE lines]. So TT hold is the binding check and sign-off (TT setup + FF hold only) would not see it. Any fix must close TT hold too; I count it as required evidence for this face.
  Three forms, cheapest first (estimates from the measured slacks):
  (a) SAME-EDGE + FACE DELAY: same-edge association + ~160-200 ps TT delay buffers on each pma_rx input at the face (about 6-8 BUF per bit, ~4k cells, local). TT hold ~+20..+60, FF hold ~+140, TT setup ~+330. No RTL, no clock, no geometry change. Needs the hold repair to target TT on these 544 paths (or an FF-side hold margin of about +130 on pma_rx->l0 only).
  (b) SAME-EDGE + SHORTER RCK: cut the stage-0 insertion by >= 180 ps TT (pin moved next to the banks as in island_plan_phy, or RX banks off the balancing chain + ~200 ps padding on q->u_dec). Bigger: plan event or a hop to pad.
  (c) NEGEDGE stage 0 (DH73 variant): needs insertion <= ~300 TT, so it only works with the F1 short branch; RTL change + lock-step proof. Most work.
  ASK (TOK/COORD): with same-edge capture, silicon takes pma_rx one rck cycle EARLIER than zero-delay RTL sim says (data of edge k sampled at edge k after ~830 ps of tree). The data then crosses into clk through the 8-deep gray-pointer rate-match FIFO (async, already +-1 cycle), so I expect no functional or schedule effect. DEFAULT after 30 min: accepted; I prepare form (a) as hd_serdes_vA (SDC pad_clock same_edge on data_inputs + face delay), with form (b) as vB estimate only, review before any build. No build launched. Same eye arithmetic applies to any pad-clock data input whose capture tree is near one period (S81-RCK-2: please check your rxm data face with it).

The planner must not move a register across ports (that would change the netlist), so on its own roots it finds 0 pairs on the 4 small roots and moves 1028 pins on the clk root. That only shifts the clk root's balance against the other roots: -10 ps. So the DIE-HBM-87 class (*__ot_q -> bank _d, about 120 ps on vCF1d) is a PORT-TO-PORT insertion-alignment class (core_tap_align / per-port insertion), not a tap class. The need is 2 x 1104 = 2208 b per half-row cut, i.e. 0.18 of supply (gate 0.6). The binding constraint is REACH plus the pushdown rule. C cell to station column is 2885.8 um = 7.1 x the 405-um registered hop (METHODOLOGY 12.1e plans 405 on every layer incl. M8/M9; physical M8 reach ~1000 um is still < 2886). So each lane needs >= 7 registers between C and the column, and 12.1d/12.2b put them in partition-owned repeater bays inside the leaves (no die std cells; 12.2a islands are clock/reset only). "Stations only at the station columns" is therefore impossible, while "thin repeater islands" = in-leaf bays (3-4 per leaf, 2208 flops each, M8->M7 entry pins per 12.7) is RULE-LEGAL (12.1c die-top nets may use leftover M8/M9). The only open risks are 12.5's pin-stack hot spots (4416 stacks per bay) and flow support: the x lanes become die-top nets with in-leaf bays instead of partition ft slots (bind/ports/kit change, S7 tooling).

For the 15 um gap: OT_GUTTER_BLOCK_UM=20 (MIN_SPAN about the core height or unset). Neither has been run on this type. STRUCTURAL ORDER for the LP type: (1) positions form (A) from my table (open a >= 41-60 um channel by moving ln1+lnl1 east, 0 cycles) is the structural fix; (2) gutter_block 20 um is the generator-level guard so any 15 um core-to-core gap becomes a placement blockage on every kit gen (the same class would otherwise recur on the other types with close cores); row-sliver >=16 is the blunter fallback.   - smh_static_front: 649-861
  - smh_pt_w: 570-577

  250 TT / 202.5 FF is the die-wide METHODOLOGY 12.3 default (clk_aocv_qc CORE_LAT, core_family_slice BAND), and no HBM density-tap core meets it. The contract is stale against the built form, but it does not drive the padding.
  Structural fix, as a class:
  (1) core_tap_align target = p90 of the logic-root tap means (taps with real sink counts), not the global r0 max.
      - Taps above the target are reported as OUTLIER and fixed in core_density_taps: re-home or split the outlier's sinks instead of padding every other tap up to it.
      - Macro-only and side roots align to the same robust target.
      - On v32e0 this removes the ~210 ps outlier pad from every tap.
      - Owner: HBM-CORES-B, on a branch, proven by a read-only replay on the v32e0 CTS db.
  (2) Trunk: clk_leaf_repeat must skip nets above the ot_dtap level (clknet_*_clk trunk, delaynet_*, CTS wire nets).
      - This belongs to CLK-LEAF-BAL-1's class.
      - Here it is ~128 ps of the 430 ps trunk, and the likely source of the outlier.
  (3) Contract: per-core contract, not the die default.
      - The plan carries parent_budget core taps at the core's measured tap median. core_clock_contract.plan_budget already reads them; compact_coll_form already uses 405/340.
      - The parent tree delivers the face clock to match; die STA on real views checks the pair. This is the industry form: characterized core latency, parent compensates.
      - Alternative: keep 202.5 and build root-driven shallow trees. No current HBM core does this.
      - Choice: DIE-HBM-100 / plan owner.
  While vclk FF stays at 202.5, (1)+(2) alone will not close port hold on these cores.

Causes: one serial train; a full main-vs-tip suite (~8.9k tests) per train; any pairwise conflict (mostly tools/die_plan/check.py) bounced back to the author for a rebase, which costs a full cycle; serial bisect.   (4) Parallel bisect.

  CAUSE, two parts:
  (1) Clock root crosses the macro. 198.72 x 198.72 die, ONE macro (ot_sram_1r1w_64x512, 171.3 x 77.8) at (8.64, 8.65), M1-M4 OBS, run at MAX_ROUTING_LAYER M5. The clock entry pin is at the die centre (99.4, 99.4), above the macro. CTS puts the root buffer clkbuf_0_clk (BUFx24) at the macro clk pin (die y 6.2, below the macro; the macro clk pin is at its local y 0.77) and its driver wire14322 at (51.6, 88.6) above the macro. So ONE two-pin clock net, net14321, crosses the whole macro. It is 14,989 of the 43,470 overflow (34%) and 5,100 of the 5,229 in the (100,20)-(120,40) hotspot. This is the same class as hbm-vecd4ae-grt-class: a clock crossing a macro where M5 capacity is 0. It is not a pin wall.
  (2) Data funnel through the side channels. 86% of the overflow sits at y < 80, over/next to the macro; the hot cells besides the hotspot are (0,60) 5043, (100,60) 4313, (0,40) 3063, (0,80) 2488. The macro pins are M4 on its left and right faces and its 1024 rd/wd bits span only y 1.5-76.8 of the macro. The die W (512 'sum') and E (512 'pv_y') M4 pins span the whole height y 2.2-196.5, and the logic is above the macro. So ~1024 nets have to climb through an 8.6 um (left) / 18.8 um (right) channel on M5 only. The top nets are u_fcore.st_rd[*]. Part (2) is not addressed by part (1) alone.

(2) pv_merge: 1024 data nets climb through narrow side channels, because the die W/E pins span y 2.2-196.5 while the macro pins sit in y 8.7-86.4. pvm_F1 (MX flip) and pvm_F2 (M7) run in parallel as core-local forms. Proposal: a plan pin event that spreads ccw_in and ccw_out (about 4400 pins) evenly over the east face to at most 42-50% of M4 tracks, with the neighbouring core's facing pins moved to match. Pin cycles and logic stay unchanged, and the cores are only moved, not re-shaped. It is not on the frozen-plan list, which allows only the tap split, the M8 grant and the conditional su area, so I am posting it for the owner and applying nothing. For pv_merge the pin window is a fallback only if F1 and F2 fail. Recommendation: YES for gnw_ccw, as one more item in the single fix event. Default if no answer: WAIT, with DIE-LAYOUT-HBM drafting the pin delta on paper.

Alternative: grow the outline by 293.76 um per type, which grows the die by about 294 um across the top row. Recommendation: YES to the move and flip for NC and NW as one more item in the single fix event, after HBM-GEOM-2 confirms the PHY position has no die-level constraint (bumps, HBM stack site). Default if no answer: WAIT, with HBM-GEOM-2 drafting the delta on paper.

The LEF the failing kit actually used (cbx_q10 attempt_3 gen/macros/qfd_tile_nk_a0c.lef, md5 cac85f89..., +372 bytes) is a detail form: M1-M5 still blanket, M6 cut by a 0.218 x 0.16 um hole (x 228.897..229.115, y 578.692..578.852, centred 0.034 off the pin) and M7 by 0.160 x 0.896 (x 228.944..229.104). HEAD routed-tree seam FF hold (-100.5 ps, 18 groups): where each group launches and why the number jumped from -12.8.
- Launch side of the 18 negative seam groups (run_tree; hd_spn_end was still a stand-in in that run):
  - sp5 = hd_spn_end (ot_s81hd_spn_end_strip): sp5->sp5_xw_o_shim/link_i -100.5 and sp5->sp5_xe_o_shim/link_i -21.3.
  - ot_s81hd_spn_strip stand-ins, sp0..sp4 -> *_xw/xe_o_shim/link_i (10 groups): xw -84.0/-66.2/-62.7/-54.3/-40.9; xe -50.9/-32.8/-30.6/-19.7/-8.1.
  - mesh_ep stand-ins -> *_estrip/m_rx_ft_i: mesh7S -46.5, mesh7N -46.3, mesh0S -40.6.
  - ctl stand-in -> ctl_estrip/n_tx_ft_i: -38.3.
  - wshim_rx stand-in sp0_bw_i_shim -> sp0/bw_i: -42.4 (both ends stand-ins).
  - host_nstrip (real) -> host_w (host_w_ep stand-in) /h_tx_i: -9.7.
  - Every capture on the shim/estrip groups is a signed view (spn_wshim_tx, spn_eshim_tx, mesh_estrip, ctl_estrip).
- Cause of the jump: the clock model's early/late split, not the stand-ins and not late-arrival skew.
  - Stand-in contract delays: same parts and contracts in the branch run and the tree run, so they do not explain the change.
  - Late skew: tree late tap arrivals match the branch spine offsets within about 2 ps (example: sp5 taps 2288-2317 vs 2287-2316).
  - Actual cause: the ASAP7 libs carry rise/fall_capacitance_range (CKINVDCx16 A 7.49..10.56 fF). OpenSTA uses the low end for min (early) analysis, so the propagated tree runs about 14 % faster early than late at the same FF corner (t_sp5__clk late 2306.8, early 1992.3 ps). CRPR cancels only the common path, and the leftover on the non-common branch segments of the launch and capture taps is the -40 to -90 ps.
  - Checked: with the *_capacitance_range lines removed, t_sp5__clk early = late = 2306.8 (head/freg/die_ctree/arr_check_FFnom.txt).
- What this means:
  - Under the nominal margin policy (OWNER 12.24b) this split is OCV-like pessimism, not a die-clock defect. The nominal routed-tree run (--libdir libs_nom, hd_spn_end real) is running now as head/ilm/run_tree2n.
  - The structural signal for HEAD-LEP0N-BAL / HEAD-94 is real: launch and capture taps of the shim seams split far up the tree, which leaves a long non-common path. Re-tapping each strip and its o_shim from one leaf branch would shrink that, so the hold result would not depend on the derate model.
- Also: die_sta ILM writer fix @2e6955a257 (tests pass). Escaped scalar nets like \fl_..._d[0] were written as bus bits, so the hd_spn_end ILM failed to parse. hd_spn_end real reruns are going: run_tree2 (lib ranges kept) and run_tree2n (nominal).

The lever is CLOCK REGION GROUPING (D7 made concrete): each heavy neighbour group shares a region root, so its hops become seam pairs with CPPR credit there. Examples: a wing column chain r0-r2, a slice row with its 2-3 leaf rows. That works under A or HFP.   CHECK 1: AGREE.
    - The hybrid lane fits damage as clock insertion skew, about 0.25 ps per um of distance from the root (r 0.99 over 20,555 taps). It reproduces all 780 rows to 0.005 ps.
    - So landed-hop damage comes from the difference in root distance of the two taps, not from hop length. My classification fits that: 384/780 are wing-internal neighbours HFP leaves alone, and only 22 are frame<->station crossings.
    - Their HFP estimate is 780 -> 744 with the root moved, 720 with it kept, about 5%. My earlier first-order B bound was 6-13%, so the two agree that geometry is not the lever.
    - The lever is the clock topology: regional roots shared by heavy neighbour groups (wing column chains r0-r2, slice + leaf bands), or a balanced feed that equalises root distance across each landed pair. HFP D7 should be specified that way and measured; channel geometry alone will not pass check 1.
  CHECK 2: AGREE that 300 um FAILS. Both cut counts are about 6-7k bits:
    - Mine, per tile: col 6 has 4997 N/S + 828 turn; col 15 has 4932 + 2052.
    - Hybrid, per cut: 6529 W, 6464 E.
    - Under the plan's own budget (face_pins_per_um 6) a 300 um channel carries 1800, so the cut needs about 1.09 mm.
    - At the G2-proven hard cap of 16 pins/um it needs about 410 um.
    - On raw ASAP7 vertical tracks (M5/M7/M9 at 50%, about 24 b/um) it needs about 290 um.
    - Recommendation: >= 450 um with a G2 proof (16 pins/um). Without a G2 proof the channel must be about 1.1 mm, and HFP's width gain falls from 2 x 1143 to 2 x about 350 um.
  ROW GRID: CONFIRMED off-grid; my offsets differ from the hybrid lane's 385-842.
    - From the D5 heights (svc lo 2850.6, svc hi 2747.5, 150-um channels) the centre row tops sit 236-536 um off the wing 1226.88 grid. My numbers: svc 397/536, leaf band A to the second channel 386, band B to the edge 236.
    - Fix: size the two horizontal relay channels to 990.6 and 1076.9 um instead of 150, which puts every leaf/slice row back on the wing grid. The centre stack grows by about 1.77 mm, which no longer fits 24.74 (24.30 + 1.77 = 26.07 mm).
    - Alternative: accept the offset and let the channels jog the frame<->centre wires (up to 613 um more per crossing).
  NET: HFP as drawn does not deliver its main claim (landed hops) and needs wider channels. I support it only together with a clock-region redesign that is measured on a trial plan.
  correction to the ROW GRID line above (S81-DIEREVIEW-1, 05:11 PST): the channel sizes that realign the rows are 536.3 um for the first channel (above svc hi; svc_hi top 6825.0 -> grid 7361.3) and 1226.88 um for the second (a full row; anything else shifts band B off-grid by its own height). That is +1.46 mm on the centre stack (24.30 -> 25.77 mm > 24.74), not the 990.6/1076.9 and +1.77 I posted. The conclusion is unchanged: either the die grows by about 1 mm in height or the channels jog the wires.

They match only if the boot issues GO on a fixed edge count after die rst_n, and the compiler anchors each slice's x words on that slice's parity. **Revised recommendation (B + guard):** (B) I compute the per-slice TX release edge (E1_s) from the bound reset tree and hand TOK-VERIFY-2 a 16-row parity table, and a boot/GO bench proves the GO issue edge is fixed after die rst_n. Then a parity slip is a reported fault, not silent corruption (no width change; the f bus gains 1 bit per slice). COORD: B+guard is the default, and I start it after the EQ RESULT unless you choose (A) instead.

(d) There is no per-edge word valid at the TX: the crs4 markers are mkq[1], constant 1 after release. No width change and no slice-type change, but it needs the exact go-tag bit position in the 1104-b x word, from whoever owns the S81 x payload format (S81-FRAME-FIX or DIE-S81-88?). (2) Slice-type output "GO seen" to the TX (re-sign of the 16 slice types; pre-approved class, but slower). (3) The compiler holds each x word on xc for 2 edges (TOK-VERIFY-2 knob). (B) PLAN/GENERATOR: put the landing band (the whole ring: slots + read side) next to its capture flops instead of at the pin face. Reading: about 110 ps of early capture on the register bars after CTS. That is clock-tap imbalance (bar flops on lightly loaded or near taps against long-latency launch), not wire hold, so this is a structural hold class, and a buffer-padding retry is not the fix. SP2 is dropped (it also missed the tap cap). SP3n2 (route on epyc4, 2 taps added on the W register bar, busiest 958) is the carried form and will tell whether the bar taps fix it. If SP3n2 stops on the same rule, the class goes to REACH-FIX-2 / the die clock owner as a bar tap latency balance item (target the register-bar tap insertion to the launch side). I am not re-running SP2.

  What it does: a visual verdict binds to (row, attempt, form fingerprint).
  - Verdict lines are read with their time.
  - A verdict given after the build started rated that build, and its form_fp is bound in autopilot/kit_wave_verdict_forms.json.
  - A verdict older than the build applies only when that build's bound form equals this build's form. Otherwise visual_hold returns "WAIT-VISUAL: ... rated an earlier build of another or unknown form ..." and the row needs its own review.
  - form_wait compares against the bound (rated) form. If there is no binding and the attempt dir now holds a newer spec, it never holds.
  - A verdict line without a time keeps the old behaviour.
  Tests: test_kit_wave_verdict_form.py, 10 cases (same form inherits; other form, unbound or GOOD-on-other-form waits for review; form_wait uses the bound form). kit_wave suite: 572 passed, 1 known baseline failure (test_own_cap_sigkill_247).

Rules: (a) The parent is chosen by GEOMETRY: the nearest face site, within hop, of a soft partition released earlier in the previous solve, pinned like reset.parent_pins. No segment under 186 um exceeds 320. Slew is wire-RC-limited (it hits BUFx16f as well), roughly quadratic, and spreads 2x at equal length by layer. Worst wire term over nets of 150 um or more: k = 0.0093 TT / 0.0103 FF ps/um^2, on top of driver slew p90 102 TT / 65 FF. Target 320/1.2 = 267 ps gives 133 TT / 140 FF, so L_safe = 130 um (SLEW_SAFE_RELAY_UM, branch 39e04ecad5, plan opt-in reset.relay_rule slew_safe). CAVEAT: the measurement is on segments. The same kits pass relay hops of 358-377 um when repair_design splits them into segments of 200 um or less, so 130 um is the hop ONE relay stage drives unbuffered. SWEEP: current plans, per type tree; die hop reach unchanged; (a) = relay spacing in a filled span; (b) = the subtree feeds only rst_o/core pins (far pin), or no data sink within 50 um inside the hop's box (empty span). HEAD 976, 91 -> 125 (+3). QC 10873, 154 -> 204 (+4). KV 6961, 79 -> 108 (+3). HBM 1928, 87 -> 113 (+13). At 190 and 250 the cost falls in between (rsw json). Every die's trees are packed at the 380 plan reach, so (a) dominates everywhere (63-87%). (b) is largest on HBM (44%) and S81 (37%); top (b) types are S81 bk_sel__t2, HEAD hd_spn, QC cbf_q01 / cbn_q00, KV kv3_pv_v12 / kv3_hub_C, HBM q_sm1. VERDICT / ASK: the 130 um default is correct as the one-stage slew-safe hop, but as a relay pitch it roughly triples release depth on every die (S81 131 -> 420, QC 154 -> 474) and adds about 600k relay flops.     - Count: autopilot.after_class keeps a kit-wave type job SIGNED with its archive pending (not counted) until its verdict is GOOD, OK or ISSUES-ACCEPT. BAD/ISSUES withholds the archive permanently.
